builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CoS-VQ: Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization for Large Language Models
summary: It replaces higher-dimensional VQ codewords and independent pointwise index updates with low-dimensional codewords whose hard indices and shared scale are jointly updated under a residual-aware quadratic surrogate. The cost is a more complex offline quantization procedure with multi-scale candidate probing, representative-interval search, likely calibration/compute overhead, and the need for deployment kernels that preserve the packed low-bit format. It can fail if the separable upper bound does not transfer across models or tasks, if hard-index changes amplify outlier-sensitive layers, or if systems integration removes the memory advantage while coding/reasoning accuracy regresses.
rationale: The method is directly relevant to fitting LLMs under a 24 GB budget, but the abstract provides only comparative quality claims without measured memory/latency factors, so adoption should follow a small workload-specific reproduction.

claims.statement: It replaces higher-dimensional VQ codewords and independent pointwise index updates with low-dimensional codewords whose hard indices and shared scale are jointly updated under a residual-aware quadratic surrogate. The cost is a more complex offline quantization procedure with multi-scale candidate probing, representative-interval search, likely calibration/compute overhead, and the need for deployment kernels that preserve the packed low-bit format. It can fail if the separable upper bound does not transfer across models or tasks, if hard-index changes amplify outlier-sensitive layers, or if systems integration removes the memory advantage while coding/reasoning accuracy regresses.

The abstract states that on Qwen3.8-27B CoS-VQ outperforms QTIP and LLVQ on the evaluated language modeling, coding, and reasoning benchmarks, and that joint updates give larger same-initialization gains than scale-only refinement; no numerical factor is reported.
